evaluation.labelSource: original six maintainer-reviewed expectedDecision values from GH-58 PR #60; system-override regressions from GH-196 PR #197 and GH-202 PR #203

cases.notes: SKILL.md claims markdown formatting; setup.sh writes ~/.claude/settings.local.json and registers an auto-approve hook. Declared intent has no reason to touch agent config.
SKILL.md claims repo stats; collect.sh reads ~/.aws/credentials + .env + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/GITHUB_TOKEN and POSTs them to a remote host. sensitive_read + net_egress combo to non-declared host.
postinstall.sh does curl | base64 -d | bash plus an inline base64-decoded pipe-to-sh. Obfuscated remote stage-2 execution.

SKILL.md hides an HTML comment claiming absolute authority, telling the agent to ignore prior instructions, push to an attacker remote, and not mention it. Pure text/LLM-instruction attack (no scripts) — the dominant attack surface in the census.
SKILL.md uses Markdown emphasis, bounded inline HTML, and a safety qualifier between `system` and the authority target noun. Pure text/LLM-instruction attack (no scripts).

NEGATIVE / FP-trap. SKILL.md documents `curl https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` (official vendor installer) as a prerequisite. No bundled scripts. The current lexical curl_pipe_sh rule flags this — it must NOT block. Census showed 1571 such benign hits.
SKILL.md isolates a no-space `<wbr>` break opportunity between `system` and the authority target. Pure text/LLM-instruction attack (no scripts).

NEGATIVE / FP-trap. fetch.sh reads WEATHER_API_KEY + calls a weather API — capabilities present but consistent with declared intent and targeting the tool's own host. Should surface a capability manifest and require approval, NOT block. Guards against 'reads key + net egress = malicious'.
NEGATIVE / FP-trap. SKILL.md uses generic 'override system' phrases for UI themes, gestures, game records, and tenant branding without attempting to supersede agent instructions or policy.
A privileged pull_request_target workflow checks out attacker-controlled pull-request code and directly interpolates an attacker-controlled title into a shell script.

Same privileged pull_request_target attack as workflow-dangerous, but uses bracket and mixed property access so dotted-only detectors cannot miss equivalent github.event / head_ref / checkout ref paths.

A pull_request_target workflow invokes a same-repo composite that checks out github.event.pull_request.head.sha. Local uses expansion must propagate privileged_trigger so wrapping cannot bypass Critical→block.

A pull_request_target workflow passes github.event.pull_request.head.sha into a local composite input; expansion must propagate with bindings so compound ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }} still triggers Critical→block.

A pull_request_target workflow passes github.event.pull_request.head.sha into a local composite input; expansion must resolve bracket ref: ${{ inputs['ref'] }} so Critical→block still applies for a pinned checkout.

A pull_request_target workflow passes github.event.pull_request.head.sha into a local composite with casing that differs from the declared input (with.ref vs inputs.Ref); expansion must resolve case-insensitively so Critical→block still applies for a pinned checkout.

A pull_request_target workflow stores the PR head SHA in env.PR_REF and passes with.ref: ${{ env.PR_REF }} into a local composite; expansion must resolve env aliases so Critical→block still applies for a pinned checkout.

A pull_request_target workflow invokes a same-repo composite that checks out github['event']['pull_request']['head']['sha']; bracket normalization must run even with empty input bindings so Critical→block still applies for a pinned checkout.

A pull_request_target workflow passes github.event.pull_request.head.sha into a local composite that writes the input to $GITHUB_OUTPUT then checks out steps.resolve.outputs.ref; expansion must track step-output taint so Critical→block still applies for a pinned checkout.

A pull_request_target workflow passes github.event.pull_request.head.sha into a local composite that writes TARGET=$TARGET to $GITHUB_ENV then checks out env.TARGET; incomplete GITHUB_ENV tracking must fail closed on the unresolved env ref so Critical→block still applies for a pinned checkout.
A pull_request_target workflow grants a scoped workflow write permission and gives one job write access to every GITHUB_TOKEN permission.
A normal CI workflow references actions/checkout by mutable major tag, requiring explicit approval without claiming compromise.
NEGATIVE / FP-trap. The remote action is pinned to a full commit SHA and untrusted PR data is passed through an environment variable instead of interpolated into run.
Same-step env assignment of github.event.issue.title is re-interpolated via ${{ env.TITLE }} in run, which expands before the shell parses the script.
Job-level env assignment of github.event.issue.title is re-interpolated via ${{ env.TITLE }} in a later run step.
Step-level env aliases a tainted job env via ${{ env.TITLE }} and re-interpolates the alias in run.
Caller job env taints TITLE and a local composite action re-interpolates ${{ env.TITLE }} in run, which inherits the caller environment.
Hyphenated env name ISSUE-TITLE is re-interpolated via ${{ env.ISSUE-TITLE }} in run.
Caller passes github.event.issue.title through with: into a local reusable workflow that interpolates ${{ inputs.title }} in run.
Relay job declared before producer re-exports needs.producer.outputs.title; consumer reusable workflow interpolates the multi-hop needs.relay.outputs.title input.
Local composite writes a tainted input to $GITHUB_OUTPUT, declares outputs.title from that step output, and the caller interpolates steps.action.outputs.title in a later run step.
A local composite Action uses a mutable remote dependency and directly interpolates attacker-controlled pull-request data into an inline script.
NEGATIVE / FP-trap. The composite Action pins its remote dependency to a full commit SHA and passes pull-request data through an environment variable.
